newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police order PLO Jerusalem offices to close.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police order PLO Jerusalem offices to close.

text.p: Israeli police said on Wednesday they had issued warnings to four Palestinian offices in East Jerusalem to close on their own accord within 96 hours or be shut down.
The PLO's top official in Jerusalem charged that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to close the offices was aimed at stirring conflict with the Palestinians.
A U.S. official described the Israeli move as "very difficult to understand".

The warnings were issued hours after an aide to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said it would be impossible for Israel to carry out a West Bank pullback due this week unless the four offices in Arab East Jerusalem close.
"It (the warning) gives them 96 hours to close down. If they don't close the offices they will be shut down," a police spokesman said, adding that Palestinians could appeal the decision.

Israel says Yasser Arafat's Palestinian self-rule Authority (PA) is conducting political activity in these offices in violation of Israel-PLO interim accords. Palestinians say the offices are not affiliated with the PA.
Witness said police glued the warnings to doors of the offices.

The police spokesman named the PLO offices as the Jerusalem Association for Welfare and Development, the National Islamic Committe Confronting Settlements, the Palestinian Institute for the Wounded and the Office of National Organisations.
The 96-hour warning gave Palestinians until Sunday to appeal, two days after the due date for Israel's withdrawal. It was not immediately clear how that would affect Israel's plans.
Cabinet ministers were scheduled to meet on Thursday to decide on the timing and scope of the pullback.

David Bar-Illan, Netanyahu's media adviser, said earlier on Wednesday that Israel intended to meet a Friday deadline to pull troops back from mainly rural areas of the West Bank but first demanded "reciprocity" from the PLO.
"It is impossible for the peace process to continue, for the redeployment and other obligations which Israel has, to continue without the closing of these offices," Bar-Illan told Reuters.

Faisal al-Husseini, responsible for Jerusalem affairs in the Palestinian Authority, said the closure orders on the heels of Israel's plan to build 6,500 more Jewish homes in the eastern part of the city, were a deliberate provocation.
"Although we see that these Israeli measures will cause an explosion, we are trying to save matters by contacting the Israelis and other countries to prevent this happening," said Husseini.

Israel Television said Netanyahu would meet with U.S. ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk on Wednesday after the United States -- Israel's biggest ally -- criticised the Jewish state for the second time in a week.

"As the President and the Secretary of State have both said, this is a time when it is very important that the (Middle East) parties take steps that will build confidence between them," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.

"It is therefore very difficult to understand why the Israeli government made such a decision at this time when there is a very difficult environment in the relationship with the Palestinians," he told reporters.
